Designing resilient layouts for the modern web

A practical walk through flexbox, grid and the quirks that make real pages harder than the specs suggest.

Layout engines make thousands of small decisions before a single pixel appears on the screen. Understanding those decisions helps you write simpler CSS and debug the odd corner cases that every project eventually meets.

Start with the box model

Every element generates a box. The box-sizing property decides whether width includes padding and borders, and most modern resets set it to border-box for good reason.

  • Content, padding, border and margin form the four layers.
  • Percentages resolve against the containing block, not the parent's font size.
  • Margins between siblings collapse; padding never does.
Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability. The less magic in the stylesheet the more predictable the result.

A short example

.card {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr;
  gap: 16px;
}

Flexible components

Flexbox excels at one dimensional arrangements such as toolbars, navigation and button rows. Grid is better suited to two dimensional structure. Combine them freely, but prefer the simplest tool that solves the problem at hand.

  1. Set display: flex on the container.
  2. Let items grow and shrink with flex.
  3. Use gap instead of margins between items.
